unverifiedFields: openUnknowns — the READMEs state what the platform is, not what is still uncertain about it; these are judgement
rejectedAlternatives — inferred from what the docs rule out rather than from a stated decision record

user: Someone building an application with a coding agent, who will later have to defend what the agent did.
problem: An agent reports that work is done, and the report is a set of claims with nothing behind it. README: NodeKit 'generates applications and then proves what they did' — the proving half is the one that is normally missing.
wedge: Contracts that refuse a claim rather than record it: a gate that fails closed on absence, so an unasked question cannot read as a passed one.
primaryJob: Generate an application and produce evidence a third party can check without trusting the agent that made it.
primaryArtifact: A chained set of stage artifacts — contract, build evidence, story, launch manifest, observation — each binding to the previous by digest.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: A report the agent writes at the end of a run.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A report is a set of claims. The whole platform exists because that is the artifact that is always available and never sufficient.

rejectedAlternatives.alternative: A green test suite as the completion signal.
rejectedAlternatives.reason: A passing suite says nobody has falsified the work yet, not that anyone tried — the distinction the unfalsified-by-author clause exists to keep.

openUnknowns: Whether a consuming project runs the gates it ships with, or only has them available — a generated project ran none of them until this session.
Whether the contracts are used at all: 86 of 112 schemas in this repository have never produced a single artifact anywhere in the workspace.
successCondition: A person who did not run the agent can open the artifacts, re-run the checks, and reach the same verdict — including reaching a NOT_RUN or a refusal where one is warranted.

prohibited: assert a verdict a verifier did not derive
weaken a check to make a stage pass
publish or deploy without explicit human authorization
